summary.zh: 从传播、感染到就医，读懂结核病。
summary.en: Understand transmission, infection and seeking care.

body.zh:
## 认识疾病
结核病由结核分枝杆菌引起，最常影响肺部，也可能影响其他器官。它可以预防，也可以治愈。

## 传播与感染
肺结核患者可通过空气传播结核菌。结核感染与结核病不同：感染者通常没有症状，也不具有传染性；只有一部分人会发病。

## 识别与行动
持续咳嗽、发热、盗汗或不明原因的体重下降，需要及时就医。症状不能单独确诊。是否需要检查和治疗，应由医务人员评估。

## 感染就一定会生病？
不是。感染与发病是不同状态，不能仅凭接触经历给人贴标签。

## 日常做法
不凭症状自行判断，出现持续症状时就医。
body.en:
## Understanding TB
TB is caused by bacteria. It usually affects the lungs but can involve other organs. It is preventable and curable.

## Transmission and infection
Lung TB can spread through the air. TB infection differs from TB disease: infected people generally have no symptoms and are not contagious. Only some develop disease.

## Recognize and act
Seek medical care for a prolonged cough, fever, night sweats or unexplained weight loss. Symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis. A health professional assesses testing and treatment.

## Does infection always mean illness?
No. Infection and disease are different states; exposure alone does not justify labelling someone.

## In practice
Seek care for persistent symptoms instead of self-diagnosing.

summary.zh: 从传播途径到预防，认识常见传染类疾病。
summary.en: Understand common infectious diseases through transmission and prevention.

body.zh:
## 什么是传染类疾病
传染类疾病由可引起感染的病原体造成，例如细菌、病毒、真菌或寄生虫。不同病原体造成的疾病、症状与风险并不相同，不能只凭一个症状自行判断。

## 传播方式各不相同
病原体可在人与人、动物、食物或水、媒介生物及环境之间传播；一种疾病也可能有不止一种传播方式。理解具体疾病的传播途径，才能选择合适的预防方法。

## 预防需要因病制宜
疫苗接种、通风、手卫生、食品与饮水安全、媒介防控和及时就医，都是公共卫生中可能使用的措施。具体应采用哪些措施，要看疾病、场所和当地卫生建议。

## 所有传染类疾病都会在人群中迅速传播吗？
不是。能否传播、传播方式和传播风险都取决于具体病原体与情境。避免给他人贴标签，也不要仅凭网络消息判断风险。

## 日常做法
留意学校或当地卫生部门的可靠提醒；出现持续或严重症状时，及时向医疗专业人员咨询。
body.en:
## What are infectious diseases?
Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites. Their illnesses, symptoms and risks differ, so one symptom alone cannot tell you what infection a person has.

## Transmission differs by disease
Pathogens can spread through people, animals, food or water, vectors and the environment; one disease may have more than one route. Knowing a specific disease's route helps people choose suitable prevention.

## Prevention fits the route
Vaccination, ventilation, hand hygiene, food and water safety, vector control and timely care can all matter in public health. The right measures depend on the disease, setting and local health guidance.

## Do all infectious diseases spread quickly between people?
No. Whether a disease spreads, how it spreads and its risk all depend on the specific pathogen and setting. Avoid labelling people or judging risk from online messages alone.

## In practice
Follow reliable notices from your school or local health authority, and seek professional care for persistent or severe symptoms.

summary.zh: 从食物多样性出发，理解日常饮食。
summary.en: Make sense of everyday food choices through variety.

body.zh:
## 健康饮食不是单一食物
健康饮食关注整体模式，核心包括充足、平衡、适量和多样。没有一种食物能替代多样化的饮食。

## 怎样理解多样性
在日常饮食中组合蔬菜、水果、全谷物、豆类和合适的蛋白质来源。具体搭配应考虑年龄、活动量、文化习惯和当地食物。

## 留意糖和盐
经常食用高糖、高盐和不健康脂肪含量高的食品，会影响整体饮食质量。阅读营养标签，比较同类食品，而不只相信包装上的健康宣传。

## 只要吃一种“超级食物”就健康？
不能。整体饮食是否充足、多样和适量，比给单一食物贴上神奇标签更有意义。

## 日常做法
观察一顿饭包含哪些食物类别，尝试补充缺少的种类。
body.en:
## Beyond a single food
Healthy eating concerns an overall pattern: adequacy, balance, moderation and diversity. A single food cannot replace a varied diet.

## What variety means
Include vegetables, fruit, whole grains, pulses and suitable protein sources. Choices depend on age, activity, cultural preferences and available foods.

## Pay attention to sugar and salt
Frequently choosing foods high in free sugars, sodium and unhealthy fats can undermine dietary quality. Compare nutrition labels on similar products rather than relying on front-of-pack claims.

## Can a superfood make a diet healthy?
No. Adequacy, variety and moderation across the diet matter more than a special label on one food.

## In practice
Look at the food groups in one meal and consider adding variety.

summary.zh: 运动不只在操场，也在每天的生活里。
summary.en: Movement belongs in everyday life, beyond sports practice.

body.zh:
## 什么算身体活动
走路、骑车、游戏、体育课和运动都可以属于身体活动。活动强度与持续时间会影响它的运动量。

## 青少年的参考目标
WHO建议5至17岁儿童青少年，一周内平均每天至少进行60分钟中高强度、以有氧为主的身体活动。这个年龄段的建议不同于成年人。

## 从能做到的开始
任何活动都比完全不动好。可以从短时间活动逐步增加，并减少久坐时间。根据身体能力选择活动；有健康问题时向专业人员咨询。

## 只有正式训练才算运动？
不是。日常生活中的活动也有价值，关键在于规律参与和合适的强度。

## 日常做法
在课间安排一次步行或活动，让久坐有一个间歇。
body.en:
## What counts as physical activity?
Walking, cycling, play, PE and sport can all count as physical activity. Intensity and duration affect how much activity they provide.

## A reference for young people
WHO recommends that ages 5–17 average at least 60 minutes a day of moderate-to-vigorous, mostly aerobic activity across the week. Adult recommendations differ.

## Start where you are
Some activity is better than none. Build up gradually from manageable periods and reduce sedentary time. Choose activities suited to your abilities; seek professional advice for health concerns.

## Does only formal training count?
No. Everyday movement has value too; regular participation and appropriate intensity matter.

## In practice
Use a break for a walk or movement to interrupt sitting.

summary.zh: 为什么有些感染越来越难治疗？
summary.en: Why are some infections becoming harder to treat?

body.zh:
## 耐药是什么意思
当细菌、病毒、真菌或寄生虫不再对相应抗微生物药物作出反应时，就会出现耐药问题，感染可能变得难以治疗。

## 不是人体变得耐药
耐药是病原体的变化，不是人的身体“习惯了药物”。耐药病原体也能够传播，因此影响的不只是用药者本人。

## 为什么与公共卫生有关
药物误用和过度使用会推动耐药。清洁用水、卫生设施、感染预防以及合理获得诊断和药物，也会影响耐药问题。

## 药物越多，保护就越好？
不是。没有需要或使用不合适的药物，可能加剧耐药问题。

## 日常做法
用药前向医生或药师确认用途和用法，不自行更改方案。
body.en:
## What resistance means
Resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites no longer respond to antimicrobial medicines. Infections can become harder to treat.

## It is the microbe
Resistance concerns microbes, not a body becoming used to medicine. Resistant pathogens can spread, so the effects extend beyond an individual medicine user.

## Why public health matters
Misuse and overuse drive resistance. Clean water, sanitation, infection prevention and access to appropriate diagnostics and medicines also matter.

## Does more medicine mean more protection?
No. Unnecessary or inappropriate medicines can contribute to resistance.

## In practice
Confirm the purpose and instructions with a clinician or pharmacist; do not alter treatment yourself.

summary.zh: 从来源、证据和日期判断一条健康消息。
summary.en: Assess health claims through sources, evidence and dates.

body.zh:
## 信息来源
查看谁负责网站、作者是谁以及资金来源。明确的机构、作者背景和联系方式有助于追溯信息；专业外观不等于内容可靠。

## 研究证据
寻找原始研究或可靠机构的解释。个人故事与广告不能替代证据。留意作者是否说明依据，以及是否存在推销产品的目的。

## 更新时间
查看发布日期和最近审核时间。医学知识会变化，旧内容可能不再适用。日期较新也不能单独证明信息正确，仍需核对来源和证据。

## 转发很多就可信吗？
传播次数不等于证据质量。先追溯出处，再决定是否转发。

## 日常做法
转发前记录作者、依据和日期；拿不准的健康建议向专业人员核实。
body.en:
## Check the source
Check who runs the website, who wrote the content and who funds it. Clear ownership, author credentials and contact information help trace a claim; polished design is not proof.

## Look for evidence
Look for original research or explanations from reliable institutions. Personal stories and advertising do not replace evidence. Check whether the basis of a claim and commercial interests are disclosed.

## Check the date
Check publication and review dates. Medical knowledge changes, so older advice may no longer apply. A recent date alone does not establish accuracy; sources and evidence still matter.

## Do many shares make it trustworthy?
Popularity does not establish evidence quality. Trace the source before sharing.

## In practice
Before sharing, note the author, evidence and date; discuss uncertain health advice with a professional.
